mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.0% per annum signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates on equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS does not decline below 2.0% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 persons indicates strong labor demand, boosting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS does not rise above 200,000 for 3 consecutive months, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly industrial production (INDPRO) above 101.0 (2017=100 baseline) reflects robust supply-side growth, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as market anticipates sustained output expansion.
failure_condition: INDPRO does not exceed 101.0 for 3 consecutive months, or 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate crosses above 4.0% per annum, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to heightened interest rate sensitivity in an already restrictive environment.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS above 4.0%, or the rate does not stay above 4.0% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 6.5% triggers positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns as improved labor market conditions boost investor confidence.
failure_condition: 5-day returns do not turn positive within 3 days of the UNRATE crossing below 6.5%, or UNRATE does not stay below 6.5% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling federal funds rates below 2.0% AND rising quarterly GDP (GDPC1) above 18000 (vintage value) creates a dual signal of monetary easing and strong demand, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both proxies meet the trigger condition, or the effect diminishes over time.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in employment (PAYEMS > 137712) and decline in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL < 235.288) signals labor market strength and deflationary pressures, amplifying positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns fail to rise significantly when both conditions are met, or the effect reverses within the period.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in FEDFUNDS above 4.0% per annum intensifies negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to heightened rate sensitivity in an already restrictive environment.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS above 4.0% in the tightening regime, or the rate does not stay above 4.0% for 3 months.
